beats.headline: One muskrat, one mother
beats.text: A hobgoblin at the Silk Road, midway through pricing hob-lobbers, mentions that she once watched her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat. To teach the warlord a lesson, her mother said; the daughter suspects another reason. A few minutes on, Princess Donut hopes the mother won't be biting her head off too. No danger, says the hobgoblin: she died. It was a vorpal muskrat. You can't bite the head off a vorpal muskrat without doing a little dying in the process. Nobody asks what vorpal means.

beats.headline: Fifteen things behind a door
beats.text: In a secret corridor of the Desperado Club, past fifty traps, some of them demon snares, is the abandoned practice arena of the defunct Demon Tamer's Guild, and in it fifteen red-tagged monsters nobody has identified. The paper sign on the padlocked door: Warning. Do Not Enter. Extreme, You're-Going-To-Die-In-A-Lot-Of-Pain Danger. Posted by Management. Parties have gone in. None came out. Carl, setting an ambush in that same corridor, walls the door off with two blast-resistant panels and sandbags, on a feeling.

beats.headline: The last resort
beats.text: A feral demon out of the Nothing is loose on the middle floor, eating guards, and the club cannot kill her. Astrid pulls the trigger: "I had to unleash the vorpals." Carl asks what those are. It does not matter, she says; they are going to kill everything, so flee or hide. Then she frets about what is taking them so long. Meanwhile, guards heading down that corridor keep landing on Carl's teleport traps. The vorpals won't go up to the top floor, she adds, not sounding sure.

beats.headline: Deputised by the gods
beats.text: Mordecai, asked in chat, has not seen these in a while. Vorpal is a condition, not a species. Feral means touched by the Nothing; vorpal means deputised by the gods, or better, turned into suicide bombers. Any race, sometimes hidden until a demon is near. Celestial guards and foot soldiers. The closer the demon, the stronger and angrier they get; they sense it, go to it, and draw its aggro. If one thinks it is losing, it explodes, and everybody in the room is dead with it. Stay away.

beats.headline: Carl opens his own wall
beats.text: The only thing between the vorpals and the club is the wall Carl built. So he sends a door-opening bot down the hidden hallway, programmed with a sixty-second delay to undo his own bracers and burrow through his own sandbags, and goes upstairs. Some minutes on, a buzzsaw sound rises through the floor of the strip club, and yellow fluid sprays through a hole in the boards. The demon screams a name, and a curse, and stops. The vorpals have found her.

beats.headline: Still loose downstairs
beats.text: The demon is dead and the vorpals are still tearing through the lower level. Now that they have bathed in demon blood they are supposed to dissipate back to the celestial realm, which is fine in theory and silent on timing. Crawler Carl keeps an eye on Damascus Steel, crying on the floor of the club, because Damascus is a demon class and his presence is a problem with those things still in the building.
